origin_result.basis: exact calculation requires a bill of materials and manufacturer declaration to verify compliance with the tariff shift (CTSH) and 45% value addition requirements.

procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism requires the factory to be registered through its Factory Registration service prior to applying for a certificate of origin, taking about 3 working days.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The Ministry of Foreign Trade provides the Certificate of Origin for India e-service on the ministry portal for registered local manufacturers and exporters to submit applications with required documents.

The issuing authority requires the application to include the HS code, description, quantity, and value for each product item separately, and may request detailed cost sheets or conduct factory visits.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee ranging from AED 10 to AED 200 depending on invoice value.
The competent authority issues the Certificate of Origin prior to, at, or within 5 working days of exportation, valid for 12 months for a single import.
The exporter must ensure goods are shipped directly from the UAE to India and indicate third-party invoicing on the claim if applicable.
The exporter must maintain origin records, including cost breakdowns, for at least 5 years from the end of the year of certificate issuance.

The Indian importer claims the preferential tariff rate when filing the bill of entry, maintains origin information under CAROTAR 2020 for at least 5 years, and reportedly uploads electronic certificates to e-Sanchit (unconfirmed).

caveats.note: No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
'+' in a rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.

Inference: a producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
